question.problem: Nicole bakes triangular cakes with a base of $5$ cm and a height of $3$ cm. What is the area of one cake?
question.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our cake based on the description.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14199152/assets/205df21c66b54b84f9b0608baebf49277720738e1fac14219a7631848ea5c19a.png)

The height and base of the triangle are

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{base} & =5, \\ \text{height} & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle can be found by the following formula:

$$
\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\times \text{base}\times \text{height}
$$

Substituting the values of the base and height, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area} & =\frac{1}{2}\times 5\times 3 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\times 15 \\  & =7.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's find the units. Since base and height are measured in centimeters, the area is measured in square centimeters. Hence,

$$
\text{Area}=7.5\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$
